# libreac / fuzz_ctrl

libreac's own fuzz target `fuzz_ctrl` ([source](source/fuzz_ctrl.c), unmodified), which OSS-Fuzz does not run, over libreac 1.9.0 (FreeREAC/libreac at d16f3f4e).

Reads the payload as our MAC, a mode byte and up to 256 length-prefixed frames, each in its own allocation, and runs every frame through libreac's control-plane parsers: reac_ctrl_parse, the checksum and head-amp record checks, the box classifier, the identity reply, the two-fragment identity reassembly and the catalogue match, and for a frame of at least 50 bytes with EtherType 0x8819 the port-table decode. When the mode byte asks, it first builds a catalogue row's blocks with reac_ctrl_build_as and parses them back.

## How this program differs from a libFuzzer build of this fuzz target
- Linked against a static libreac.a of every src/*.c of libreac 1.9.0 at commit d16f3f4e, compiled with each build's flags, as libreac's Makefile builds its fuzz targets but with this toolchain in place of a native clang and libFuzzer.
- In every build, getenv() returns NULL, getpid() returns 1 and mkstemp() uses a fixed name, so the program depends only on its input.
- A small driver reads the input file, calls the fuzz target one to four times and prints each return value.

## What the harness checks
- reac_ctrl_parse answers NONE exactly for a frame shorter than 50 bytes or not 0x8819, gives the same verdict with a NULL output, and its verdict is the kind it stores, which always has a name ([lines 285-305](source/fuzz_ctrl.c#L285-L305)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- The parser reads the addresses and counter where the frame holds them and calls a frame FILLER exactly for type 00 00; the block and head-amp record checksum checks agree with sums the harness computes, and a head-amp record is only a link-4 SINGLE ([lines 414-466](source/fuzz_ctrl.c#L414-L466)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- Both port decoders refuse the same blocks, leaving the output untouched; a decoded port table counts each slot code as its own kind in whole 4-channel slots, accounts for all twelve slots, names the first unknown code, and gives the head-amp base from the chassis strap ([lines 98-171](source/fuzz_ctrl.c#L98-L171)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- An identity reply comes only from a frame with a closed block checksum, its payload lies where the record puts it inside the frame, its record checksum closes and its address is the record's own; a reassembled record lies inside the reassembly buffer, closes its checksum and carries the joined record's own address (its bytes 9 and 10), and a corrupt frame leaves the reassembly state unchanged ([lines 310-405](source/fuzz_ctrl.c#L310-L405)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- The box classifier answers only for a Roland-OUI source that is not us, with a closed block checksum outside FILLER, and with one of its six events; only a config-announce matches a catalogue row, and it is the first row whose declaration is the frame's block ([lines 470-513](source/fuzz_ctrl.c#L470-L513)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- Every block reac_ctrl_build_as emits for a catalogue row has a legal geometry and parses back as its kind; the config block's checksum closes, it is the row's declaration, the catalogue match recognises it and it declares the row's widths; its identity replies and reassembled records give the row's firmware, REAC version and, where the row has an identity record, model name ([lines 531-653](source/fuzz_ctrl.c#L531-L653)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- The catalogue is not empty, the documented refusals of a bad argument hold (NULL pointers are refused, reac_ports_unknown clears its code, an out-of-range kind is named "?"), and an ingested model name is NUL-terminated ([lines 669-725](source/fuzz_ctrl.c#L669-L725)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.

## Builds
Static riscv64 Linux programs, compiled for RV64G and run as `<file> <input-file>`; `oft fetch libreac` downloads the published ones and checks each against its SHA-256.

| build | file | bytes | sha256 |
|---|---|---:|---|
| plain | `fuzz_ctrl.plain` | 58,072 | `c6512ced9ff6bea807fb67d79cdee1a9e30e7f0d18169594cc16487709eddf52` |
| ubsan | `fuzz_ctrl.ubsan` | 62,064 | `6f0dfa56f7107fa658c776643d812731b90da89c0d24f02e4ca59ad3a4c4911b` |
| asan | `fuzz_ctrl.asan` | 600,024 | `aac16e1fe72899697a16d67dbff08390c1096be98a2fab183e80ce995135704d` |
| asan-ubsan | `fuzz_ctrl.asan-ubsan` | 603,640 | `12136677c5cf9891b3aed0c4821499bba9dde76b0e6baadb7ac66e07e6a62c17` |

Each build also links code that no sanitizer instruments, as its link recorded it. A statement about a sanitizer build covers that code only as uninstrumented code: ASan checks no load or store made inside it, and UBSan inserts no check there.

- plain: `clang_rt.crtbegin.o` (compiler-rt), `libclang_rt.builtins.a` (compiler-rt), `crt1.o` (the C library), `libc.a` (the C library)
- ubsan: `clang_rt.crtbegin.o` (compiler-rt), `libclang_rt.builtins.a` (compiler-rt), `crt1.o` (the C library), `libc.a` (the C library)
- asan: `clang_rt.crtbegin.o` (compiler-rt), `libclang_rt.asan.a` (the sanitizer runtime), `libclang_rt.builtins.a` (compiler-rt), `crt1.o` (the C library), `libc.a` (the C library), `libunwind.a` (the C++ runtime)
- asan-ubsan: `clang_rt.crtbegin.o` (compiler-rt), `libclang_rt.asan.a` (the sanitizer runtime), `libclang_rt.builtins.a` (compiler-rt), `crt1.o` (the C library), `libc.a` (the C library), `libunwind.a` (the C++ runtime)
